title: Guardian: console audit browser with saved searches & export
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a polished audit browsing experience ("Guardian") that supports rich faceted search, cursored pagination, RBAC-aware redaction, and scalable CSV/JSONL exports. The feature must be compatible with RBAC v2 policies and surface SSO/SAML context (actor, session, IP) in query results. Exports must support streaming NDJSON for large result sets, an explicit estimated export size UI, and pre-signed secure downloads. Saved queries should version with snapshot semantics so exported results are reproducible for compliance requests.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows federated audit search across hot and nearline stores with consistent filters and schema
Server returns stable cursor tokens for pagination; clients can request page N+1 and receive deterministic order
Export endpoint supports two modes: small synchronous CSV (<10k rows) and large async NDJSON streaming with gzipped S3 link
Export and view results are RBAC-aware: fields redacted per RBAC v2 policy rules and OPA policy evaluation is logged
Saved search can be created, edited, and pinned; saved-search versions are immutable and tied to export snapshots
UI displays an estimated export size and expected time-to-complete before starting an async export
Audit traceability: every export generates an audit event (who initiated, query hash, snapshot id, download token)
tech_notes: Federated search: coordinator API will fan out to hot elasticsearch-like store + nearline Parquet/BigQuery via async workers; results merged with stable sort key (event_time, id)
Cursor design: base64 encoded cursor containing (last_seen_event_time, last_seen_event_id, shard_id, schema_version) and signed server-side to avoid tampering

Export pipeline: sync path uses /v1/audit/export?format=csv limited to 10k rows; async path creates ExportJob row, workers stream NDJSON -> gzip -> upload to S3, then create pre-signed URL with short TTL

RBAC/redaction: OPA policies run in inline evaluation for view responses; for exports run OPA at export generation time to ensure exported artifacts reflect current redaction rules; include redaction markers and policy_id in metadata
SSO/SAML context: include session_id, idp, and assertion id in UI and export metadata. Ensure PII minimization where required by compliance labels
Performance: batch fetch size tuned per store; use backpressure and retry with exponential backoff for nearline queries; add per-customer export concurrency limits
Observability: trace export jobs with trace_id linking console request -> coordinator -> worker uploads; surface metrics: export_jobs_started, export_jobs_failed, export_bytes_uploaded
Data retention: exports respect data retention/redaction windows; if a saved-search snapshot references deleted data, snapshot should include a tombstone summary
implementation_plan: API: add /api/v1/audit/search (POST) with filters, page_size, cursor, include_metadata flag; spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SEC-AUDIT-SEARCH-API
Backend: coordinator service merges results, signs cursors, enforces RBAC by calling policy-eval service (ENG-18700)
Export service: new export_jobs table + worker that streams NDJSON -> gzip -> upload; small sync CSV path reuses coordinator query path
Frontend: new Guardian audit browser route; filter builder with typed facets, saved-search creation flow and snapshot modal; Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/guardian-audit-browser
QA: create test harness with replay fixtures (synth events) and golden export diffs; load test export pipeline with 100 concurrent exports
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout: start internal-only -> beta customers -> all customers; monitor error rate and export latency dashboards
Docs: write console user guide and compliance playbook in Confluence, and add API examples in SDK docs
PRs: backend prototype PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4120; frontend skeleton PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3419
risks_and_mitigation: Large exports could stress storage/network: mitigate by chunked upload, per-tenant concurrency caps, and backpressure queues
RBAC complexity could lead to inconsistent redaction between UI and exports: ensure single source policy evaluation (policy-eval service) used by both paths
Retention/regulatory conflicts: implement snapshot tombstones and explicit export provenance to show why rows may be omitted
SSO context leakage: minimize session/token fields in exports and use short-lived pre-signed URLs; redaction applied before artifact creation
Cost spikes from nearline queries: add cost-estimation step and require explicit user confirmation for expensive exports
